sourceMathEvidence: The stem says the line x=t meets y=x²/3+1 first at P and y=−(x−2)²+5 second at Q, respectively, with A=(0,1), B=(3,4), and 0<t<3. On this interval the upward curve is below the downward curve; the image shows both curves and A/B at their common endpoints but labels the upper intersection P and lower intersection Q, reversing the stated order.
solutionMathEvidence: Let f(t)=t²/3+1 and g(t)=−(t−2)²+5=−t²+4t+1. The vertical separation is g−f=−(4/3)t²+4t>0 for 0<t<3. Splitting PAQB along PQ, the two triangle heights to x=t are t and 3−t, so its area is (1/2)|PQ|t+(1/2)|PQ|(3−t)=(3/2)(g−f)=−2t²+6t=−2(t−3/2)²+9/2. Thus the maximum occurs at t=3/2 with value 9/2, matching the requested values. The P/Q swap between text and figure/solution changes orientation/labels but not the four-vertex area or this formula.

primaryMethod.label: Model the vertical gap between the two quadratic graphs, then use the shared vertical diagonal to express quadrilateral area as a one-variable quadratic.
primaryMethod.reason: The gap gives |PQ|; the left/right horizontal distances from A and B to x=t add to the fixed width 3, so the area is 3|PQ|/2.

decisiveStep.reason: Area simplifies to S(t)=−2t²+6t=−2(t−3/2)²+9/2, and t=3/2 lies in the open domain (0,3).

independentL3ChallengeReview.reason: This active type exactly fits maximizing a geometry-derived area as a function of t.
independentL3ChallengeReview.challengeAssessment: Moderate: derive the graph gap, convert the quadrilateral area, then maximize a concave quadratic on a bounded interval.

crossConceptKeys.reason: The two graph equations supply the vertical coordinates and their difference.
The quadrilateral area is computed by splitting along PQ into two triangles with horizontal heights t and 3−t.

crossConceptSelectionReason: CC_QUADRATIC_EXTREMUM and CC_VERTEX would duplicate the primary PT_FUNCTION_EXTREMUM optimization step; the broader CC_AREA is unnecessary because CC_TRIANGLE_AREA is the precise supporting geometry concept.

conditionKeys.reason: The open restriction 0<t<3 defines the admissible vertical slice and confirms the maximizing value t=3/2 is allowed.

conditionSelectionReason: The range is explicitly needed to establish the branch ordering/positive vertical gap and the admissibility of the maximizer.

integrationPattern.reason: Evaluate both graphs at x=t → form PQ → decompose area into two triangles → maximize the resulting quadratic.

sourceIssue.reason: By “respectively,” the stem assigns P to the lower upward parabola and Q to the upper downward parabola, but the diagram and solution label upper P/lower Q. Swapping P,Q reverses the boundary traversal of the same four vertices, and the area formula depends only on |PQ| and t+(3−t), so the numeric answer is unaffected.

imageEvidence.inspection: Viewed the original PNG. The upward parabola is labeled y=x²/3+1, the downward parabola y=−(x−2)²+5; A is at their left intersection and B at their right intersection. The vertical x=t line cuts the upper/downward graph and lower/upward graph, marked P and Q respectively in the image; this reverses the stem’s “respectively P,Q” assignment. The graph shapes and endpoint coordinates otherwise match the stated functions.
